title: Avalon Logistics - inference degradation bridgecall + action sprint kickoff
summary: Post-incident bridgecall to align on root cause hypotheses for a mid-April inference latency degradation, confirm mitigations, kick off a two-week action sprint for reliability and compliance items (runbook updates, KMS verification, fallback tuning), and schedule benchmark run with dedicated capacity test.
topics: Observed latency spike and tail latency
Security artifacts (KMS, audit logs, SOC2 evidence)
action_items: Marco Ruiz - collect pod-level logs for the 2025-04-15 02:00-04:00 UTC window and upload to shared folder - due 2025-04-24
Sanjay Patel - run 3-tier synthetic benchmark (short/med/long seq) on Redwood Dedicated staging and share results - due 2025-04-28
Jordan Reyes - share updated runbook draft and fallback decision checklist - due 2025-04-25
Maya Chen - send Avalon security pack (SOC2 attestation, KMS integration doc, RBAC guide) and pricing options for a 3-month pilot - due 2025-04-23
Priyanka Rao - confirm internal stakeholder window for pilot (data, legal, infra) - due 2025-04-24
next_steps: Redwood to provision Dedicated staging with identical model v1.3 config (quantized) for benchmark

Schedule 60m deep-dive on fallback flows with infra + SRE (week of 2025-04-28)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Sanjay (SE), Jordan (CSM), Ellen (Avalon VP Eng), Marco (SRE), Talia (Security), Priyanka (PM)

Auto-summary: Quick bridgecall after the April 15th inference degradation incident. Goal: align on what we think happened (KV cache thrash + autoscaler mis-evaluations), confirm short-term mitigations, and start a two-week action sprint to harden fallbacks and telemetry.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for carving out time today, appreciate it. quick note, this is a follow-up from the postmortem notes you and Jordan shared — we wanted to run through the hypotheses and lock owners.
[00:22] Ellen (Avalon): yeah thanks. we had a pretty big tail latency spike mid-April that impacted our chat assistant during peak. customers saw timeouts and some 500s.
[00:37] Marco (Avalon SRE): the spike started around 02:12 UTC on the 15th and lasted about two hours; from infra view we saw pod churn and a bunch of KV cache evicts — honestly it looked like memory pressure triggered eviction but not the usual pattern.
[01:05] Sanjay (Redwood SE): ok, interesting — when you say KV cache evicts, do you mean the prefix cache on the inference nodes or your side cache?
[01:18] Marco: inference nodes, the LRU started moving aggressively. also our autoscaler backfilled new pods but they came up cold and then the model warm-up inflated latency.
[01:35] Talia (Security): just to flag from our side, we need to keep the logs for the 30-day window for compliance; will need proof of access patterns and who pulled keys.
[01:50] Jordan (CSM): noted — we'll make sure audit logs are preserved. Maya, did we have a fallback policy firing during that window?
[02:02] Maya: we saw a mix — the hosted tier fallback did kick but because you were on the hybrid routing policy some traffic still hit the dedicated pool which was struggling. so partial fallback but not full.
[02:30] Priyanka: timeline question — we think the first customer report was 02:20 UTC, so there might be 8 minutes of badness before escalations.
[02:45] Ellen: correct, our front-end retried a couple times and that compounded load, not ideal.
[03:02] Sanjay: hypothesis A: KV cache thrash due to a burst of long-sequence requests that didn't hit the same prefixes; hypothesis B: autoscaler heuristics triggered scale-down earlier than they should have because requests looked short in the previous window. both combine to create cold starts and high tail latency.
[03:25] Marco: that matches what we see. question: does Redwood's runtime do any proactive KV or prefix prefetch on warmups?
[03:40] Sanjay: currently we rely on continuous batching and warm KV reuse but we don't prefetch full prefixes on new pod create — warmup relies on reuse from prior requests. long-term we can add pre-warm scripts in the init container to seed common prefixes.
[04:05] Ellen: is that something we can do short-term? the immediate pressure is to avoid the same customer-visible SLA hits.
[04:13] Maya: short term mitigations we propose: 1) bump the min replicas on the Dedicated pool for the pilot window, 2) tune autoscaler window to a longer lookback to avoid premature scale-downs, 3) enable broader fallback so that more traffic falls back to the hosted model if dedicated latency exceeds threshold.
[04:38] Priyanka: cost implications? raising min replicas will increase committed spend.
[04:45] Maya: yes there is a cost tradeoff. we'll include pricing options for the pilot — we can do an interim burst credit to offset immediate costs.
[04:57] Talia: from a security angle, we need to validate KMS rotations and make sure the staging Dedicated nodes have the same KMS identity so access logs map. also RBAC and SSO mapping were slightly different in the pilot last month.
[05:20] Jordan: action: I will get the runbook draft that includes KMS checklists and the fallback decision tree.
[05:30] Marco: one more data ask — can Redwood replay the exact traffic against a staging Dedicated to reproduce? we can provide a redacted replay set.
[05:41] Sanjay: yes, please — if you can share the replay set (anonymized) we can run it and instrument the kernel selection and KV eviction metrics. we'll also run with and without quantization to see behavior.
[06:05] Priyanka: there's also a config difference: our prod had sequence length cap at 2,048 but the pilot used 1,024 in a few routes — not sure if mixed config caused mismatch.
[06:20] Sanjay: mixing caps can cause unexpected memory patterning, yep. we should align configs for the replay.
[06:28] Ellen: can you also check if any model updates happened around April 14–15? our product team shipped a tweak to the prompt that increased avg tokens per request.
[06:40] Maya: we've got logs that show an uptick in average tokens per request correlate with the window; that will be in the artifact Jordan shared.
[06:55] [08:00] (Speaker label blip) Unknown: there was some crosstalk; apologies if any attribution is off.
[08:12] Marco: operational ask — we need better burn charts for KV usage and a clearer alert when eviction rate crosses X per minute.
[08:25] Jordan: Redwood console can emit a custom alert; we'll propose thresholds.
[08:35] Sanjay: technical deep-dive note — the runtime's kernel selector can oscillate under memory pressure leading to slower quantized paths being chosen; we'll instrument and share a flamegraph.
[09:05] Talia: about audits — do you have the audit log retention policy for the Dedicated nodes in VPC mode? we need to confirm it's searchable for legal.
[09:17] Maya: yes, we retain audit logs for 30 days by default, with archive options for longer retention. I'll include the export steps in the security pack.
[09:30] Priyanka: OK so tactical plan and owners?
[09:36] Maya: propose a two-week sprint: week 1 — repro and benchmark, runbook updates, KMS verification; week 2 — pilot with raised min replicas and tuned autoscaler, validate fallback thresholds, and handover to ops. owners as in the action items list.
[10:00] Ellen: that sounds reasonable. any blockers for replaying traffic? Marco: we need to sanitize PII and ensure tokens are redacted.
[10:12] Sanjay: we'll give a scrub checklist for the replay format.
[10:20] Marco: also want to test a canary that forces fallback earlier so we don't see partial fallback states. can Redwood support a forced-fallback route for the test?
[10:35] Sanjay: yes, we can flip routing to prefer hosted for a subset or force the fallback for synthetic traffic. that's part of the benchmark matrix.
[10:48] Priyanka: and timelines — can Redwood have the staging Dedicated ready by end of week?
[10:55] Maya: we can provision staging Dedicated in 48 hours; we'll need the replay set and confirmation of model v1.3 and config.
[11:06] Jordan: I'll follow up with the runbook and a link to the shared folder.
[11:12] Talia: one compliance item — can you confirm HSM vs KMS usage? our compliance team requires HSM-backed for keys used in production routing.
[11:25] Sanjay: Redwood supports KMS integrations; for HSM-backed keys we can integrate with your cloud provider or customer-managed HSM if you run Private. for Hosted, we use KMS with customer-managed keys where available. we'll include a diagram in the security pack.
[11:45] Ellen: good. on the fallback decision tree — we need explicit latency thresholds and a runbook step that says when to raise min replicas.
[11:58] Maya: agreed, that will be formalized in the runbook.
[12:10] [20:00] (skipping forward)
[20:22] Sanjay: about kernel selection, we noticed under long-tail requests some quantization-friendly kernels actually underperform for certain sequence lengths; we'll test both int8 and int4 paths during the benchmark.
[20:40] Marco: that would be useful; if int4 unexpectedly causes higher GC or memory churn that's a problem.
[20:50] Priyanka: is there any immediate firewall or network policy change we should be aware of? we saw a transient connection drop in the logs.
[21:03] Sanjay: network drops could exacerbate cold starts if in-flight prefix cache drops; we'll correlate tcp resets with eviction spikes.
[21:20] Talia: from security ops, we want to verify egress rules during the incident — who made outbound connections for model telemetry?
[21:32] Jordan: we'll include that telemetry map in the deliverables.
[21:45] Ellen: ok, walk me through the pilot pricing/credit — Priyanka asked earlier about short-term cost mitigation.
[21:55] Maya: propose a 4-week pilot with a commitment to a minimum pool for two weeks, Redwood will offer a one-time pilot credit that covers 50% of the incremental cost for week 1. full pricing sent in follow-up.
[22:12] Priyanka: acceptable if we can see clear success criteria.
[22:18] Maya: success criteria: reproduce the degradation in staging and show mitigation reduces 95th/99th percentile latency by at least 60% during synthetic bursts; verify no KV eviction spikes and fallback fires predictably.
[22:36] Marco: also we need <1% client error rate during peak in the pilot.
[22:44] Maya: noted.
[22:50] [30:00] (closing items)
[30:12] Jordan: recap of immediate actions: Jordan to share runbook, SRE to upload replay, Redwood to spin up Dedicated staging, Sanjay to run benchmark, Maya to send security pack and pricing.
[30:35] Ellen: timeline checkpoint — we'll aim for initial benchmark results by 2025-04-28.
[30:42] Priyanka: theater of ops — we'll have our infra folks on standby for the test next Tues/Wednesday.
[31:00] Talia: final ask — when you send the security pack, also include sample audit logs with redaction so our legal team can see format.
[31:12] Maya: will do.
[31:20] Marco: small note — the logs we uploaded had a weird time-synch offset, you might see a few minutes shift.
[31:28] Sanjay: we'll take that into account.
[31:35] Ellen: anything else?
[31:40] Maya: no, thanks all. next steps are as recorded and we'll reconvene after benchmark.
[31:50] (call ends)

Questions recorded in meeting:
- What precise autoscaler heuristics caused premature scale-down? (Sanjay/Redwood to instrument)
- Are audit logs and KMS access records complete and searchable for compliance? (Maya to provide pack)
- Can we reproduce the eviction pattern in staging with replayed traffic? (Marco & Sanjay)
